judgment.rationale: First endpoint (Grade 1, Term 3, Listening and Speaking (Oral), sub-strand 'Daily / Weekly activities in all areas of language and other subjects'): 'Understands and uses appropriate language of different subjects' — subject-specific oral register and vocabulary, tagged 'oral language, subject language, vocabulary'. Second endpoint (Grade 2, Term 3, Listening and Speaking (Oral), sub-strand 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities'): 'Uses appropriate language with different people such as interviews different people' — tagged 'appropriate language, audience, interviews, speaking'. The two share a genuine instructional construct — choosing language appropriate to the communicative context in spoken interaction — so there is useful, pair-specific coherence, not merely overlapping tokens ('appropriate', 'different', 'language', 'uses'). But they vary along different dimensions (subject domain register vs. interlocutor/audience register plus an interview task), and the first endpoint's own Learning Component metadata records the identical subject-language statement under additional ancestor paths, including one headed by the Grade 2 banner faeff8d5-de39-5d54-932f-e4e224b1b189, showing that strand continues in parallel at Grade 2 rather than being extended by the audience-register bullet. The bounded evidence therefore shows complementary, coexisting oral-language skills — meaningful reinforcement without a justified developmental dependency — so symmetric relatesTo is chosen over buildsTowards, with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Limitations: both endpoints omit 24 source-evidence items, the first endpoint's supporting LC evidence is truncated, and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context that was inspected but cannot be independently resolved here.

The recurrence is nonetheless meaningful sustained reinforcement of the same oral convention within the same Skill Area, which supports symmetric relatesTo with canonical endpoint order and null direction.
